To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the performance of visual object recognition systems is highly dependent on the imaging conditions in which the training data were collected and (2) it is possible to adapt models acquired in a specific visual domain to new domains by learning an affine transformation of the original feature distribution.

we introduce a new method for adapting object models to new domains, that we show that our method can be successfully used to improve object recognition, and that we present a new multi domain database that can be used for future domain adaptation research.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel domain adaptation technique that improves object recognition in new imaging domains.
we present a new method for domain adaptation and show its ability to improve the performance of object recognition algorithms in a new domain.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the performance of object recognition systems can be significantly improved if we are willing to assume that the object models are valid in a broader set of domains than the one they were acquired from.
it is possible to transfer object models learned in one domain to another, and this can improve the accuracy of object recognition in the new domain.
domain shift in the visual domain can be effectively handled by learning a transform to align the feature distribution of the source and target domains.
